   ICA refutes Malaysian media report of power outage at Woodlands Checkpoint

 The Star reported that a “massive power outage at the Woodlands Checkpoint in Singapore” led to a heavy traffic jam leading to the Malaysian checkpoint.
 PHOTOS: KOO QIN YU/FACEBOOK, SCREENGRAB FROM CHECKPOINT.SG

 Published   Nov 05, 2026, 02:05 PM

 Set as preferred source Listen Summarise 中文 ICA said there was no power outage at Woodlands Checkpoint on Nov 4. It said planned electrical maintenance took place at the Old Woodlands Checkpoint from 10am to 2pm.
 Some Singapore-bound cargo traffic built up on the Causeway during the works, but lorry clearance continued at Woodlands Checkpoint. Operations at the Old Woodlands Checkpoint resumed at about 4pm.
 ICA said two lorries broke down on the Malaysian side of the Causeway, blocking one lane and causing long queues. It posted Facebook advisories and said the congestion worsened during the evening peak.
 AI generated
 SINGAPORE – There was no power outage at the Woodlands Checkpoint on Nov 4 , the Immigration and Checkpoints Authority (ICA) said, refuting a Malaysian media report of a disruption at the key border crossing.
 On Nov 4, Malaysian daily The Star reported that a “massive power outage at the Woodlands Checkpoint in Singapore” led to a heavy traffic jam leading to the Malaysian checkpoint. It said that the issue started at about noon.
 In response to queries from The Straits Times, ICA said on Nov 5 that planned electrical maintenance works were conducted at the Old Woodlands Checkpoint on Nov 4, from 10am to 2pm.
 While the Old Woodlands Checkpoint was temporarily unavailable for the clearance of arriving lorries during the works, lorry clearance continued at Woodlands Checkpoint , ICA said.
 During this period, some Singapore-bound cargo traffic built up on the Causeway, ICA said, adding that operations at the Old Woodlands Checkpoint resumed at around 4pm that day.
 ICA said that later in the day, it observed that two lorries broke down on the Malaysian side of the Causeway towards Singapore at about 4.30pm and 6.30pm respectively.
 The breakdowns blocked one of the three arrival lanes, contributing to traffic queues extending from the lorry breakdown sites into Malaysia , the authority added.
 The congestion was exacerbated by the higher volume of vehicles during the evening peak period , ICA said.
 The first lorry was removed only at 9.50pm that evening, ICA said , adding that the second was removed at about 12.20am on Nov 5.
 ICA said: “During this period, traffic towards Woodlands Checkpoint was disrupted.
 “ICA posted advisories on its Facebook page to alert travellers to the vehicle breakdowns and expected delays, and notify them when the affected lane reopened.”
 The authority’s response comes after Malaysian news outlet The Star, in its article headlined “ Power outage at Woodlands Checkpoint triggers massive Causeway gridlock ”, attributed the long queues to a power outage.
 Its report added: “Although all counters were operating at optimum level at the Bangunan Sultan Iskandar Customs, Immigration and Quarantine complex (BSI) here, the jam lasted for many hours due to a build-up of vehicles from the Singapore side.”
 It also reported that at press time, “it remains unclear what caused the power outage in Singapore”.
 Singapore’s land border crossings with Malaysia – at Tuas and Woodlands – are among the busiest in the world.
 According to ICA statistics released in February , close to 245 million travellers passed through Singapore’s checkpoints in 2025 , surpassing the 230 million seen in the previous year .
 ICA then said that around three in four travellers had entered the country through the land checkpoints.
 More recently, ICA said on Nov 1 that during the recent school holidays from Sept 4 to Sept 14, more than 6.1 million travellers crossed the two checkpoints , with the volume peaking at more than 599,000 on Sept 4 .
 The authority said that figure set a new single-day record, which surpassed the previous peak of more than 598,000 crossings on June 19.
 ICA’s response comes after some media agencies reported that heavy traffic was caused by a power outage at Woodlands Checkpoint.
